_comment: One-line description per chain slider for the generated parameter list (English). Kept in step with chain-slider-notes.ja.json: a slider added to a chain needs a line in both. A slider with no entry shows an em dash.

notes.advanced_sliders: On shows every detailed parameter below in the menu. Leave it off to work with the macros alone.
notes.ambient_color: The bare colour of unexcited phosphor. A real tube with nothing drawn is not black but a grey-green or grey-blue.
notes.ambient_level: How bright that is (x0.001). The default 1 means 0.001.
notes.ambient_mask: Whether ambient light goes through the mask. 1 = through it (on a real tube the unexcited phosphor is seen through the mask too), 0 = flat.
notes.analytic_glow: Glow strength from the analytic line, applied to every vector whether overloaded or not. The single most effective slider in this chain.
notes.analytic_glow_width: Its radius in pixels. The monochrome maximum of 160 is wide, to express the spread of a long-persistence tube.
notes.beam_flash_gain: How much brighter than the decay curve a just-struck pixel emits (the phosphor's fast initial component). Nothing happens at all when beam_flash_ms is 0.
notes.beam_flash_ms: How long a just-struck pixel emits above the decay curve (the phosphor's fast initial component). 0 disables it entirely.
notes.beam_jitter: Instability in the supply and deflection. Moves beam energy and position together by a small amount. 0 is off.
notes.beam_jitter_hz: How fast the jitter moves. Low values undulate, high values look grainy.
notes.beam_jitter_saturation_curve: How sharply the jitter falls off. Larger drops it faster.
notes.beam_jitter_saturation_range: The energy span over which the jitter falls away completely.
notes.beam_jitter_saturation_start: The energy at which the jitter starts to weaken. Brighter draws shake less, as the supply holds up.
notes.beam_peak_nits: Peak luminance of the beam core in nits. Scaled by [M] Beam Brightness.
notes.beam_width_max: The widths, in pixels, of a dim line and a bright line. Energy moves between these two.
notes.beam_width_min: The widths, in pixels, of a dim line and a bright line. Energy moves between these two.
notes.beam_width_overmax: How far energy past the threshold is allowed to widen the beam - how many times the min-to-max span it may add.
notes.beam_window_scale: The window width as a multiple of real time. Raising it widens one window, and once a window covers the whole sweep the feature is meaningless (reported as inert).
notes.bezel_glow_curve: The width and falloff of the bezel emission.
notes.bezel_glow_strength: Emission from the bezel (the surround). Gated by [M] Monitor/Glass Sim.
notes.bezel_glow_width: The width and falloff of the bezel emission.
notes.bezel_long_reflection: How much of a long stroke's light the bezel returns.
notes.bezel_long_threshold: The boundary between long and short, in window pixels. A segment longer than this counts as long.
notes.bezel_short_reflection: How much of a short stroke's light the bezel returns. The default 0.1 is there to keep text out of the bezel.
notes.bright_normal_cap: The ceiling ordinary brightness reaches in SDR. There is no such limit in HDR (fixed at 1.0 while HDR/EDR is active).
notes.bright_sigmoid: An S-curve applied on top of the power curve. Positive = sharper contrast, negative = gentler, 0 = off.
notes.bright_sigmoid_center: The inflection point of the S-curve. Vectrex's 0.8 confines the effect to the bright end.
notes.bright_threshold: The drive at which brightness saturates; energy above it goes into width instead. Colour's 0.9 barely saturates, monochrome and Vectrex at 0.5 send half of it to width.
notes.cap_no_persist: At 1, short-dwell junction dots go to a dedicated no-persist buffer instead of the phosphor pool.
notes.cap_ramp_only: Limits line-end treatment to the termini the driver flagged as RAMP.
notes.chroma_a: Primaries given as CIE xy chromaticity (when primary_color_mode is 0).
notes.chroma_b: Primaries given as CIE xy chromaticity (when primary_color_mode is 0).
notes.chroma_c: Primaries given as CIE xy chromaticity (when primary_color_mode is 0).
notes.chroma_y_gain: Each primary's luminance contribution (Y). The default [0.2124, 0.62, 0.1] is close to the Rec.709 luminance coefficients.
notes.converge_blue: Blue beam misregistration - how far the whole picture is translated, in pixels.
notes.converge_green: Green beam misregistration - how far the whole picture is translated, in pixels.
notes.converge_red: Red beam misregistration - how far the whole picture is translated, in pixels.
notes.convergence_global_coverage: The extent of that bleed, drawn as a ring with two boundaries rather than a plain blur, so a thick convergence ring can be expressed.
notes.convergence_global_gain: Not the misregistration itself but the desaturated bleed it causes: three primaries that do not quite coincide leave a whitish halo around bright areas.
notes.core_flat: Breaks the link between width and blur. Normally sigma = width/3.2, so a beam widened by overdrive becomes one broad soft mass.
notes.core_overlap_max: How direct overlap of cores is handled (0/1).
notes.defocus: Blur amount per axis (a vec2), applied uniformly across the face. The electron beam's spot size itself.
notes.dot_no_persist_dwell: The dwell threshold in microseconds used by the test above. Anything shorter is routed to the no-persistence path.
notes.edge_defocus: Astigmatism from deflection angle. The further from centre, the more obliquely the beam lands, so the spot stretches into an ellipse and blurs.
notes.edge_defocus_curve: How the effect bends with distance from centre. Larger means nothing near the middle and a sudden onset at the edges.
notes.edge_glow: The strength of the emission. Default 0.75.
notes.edge_glow_length: The length of the emission along the edge, in pixels.
notes.edge_glow_persist: Temporal smoothing, default 120 ms. Without it the edge blinks frame by frame as the beam crosses in and out.
notes.edge_glow_sensitivity: Sensitivity to how far the beam swings off screen - the deeper it goes the brighter it glows, and this is the conversion.
notes.edge_glow_threshold: The minimum energy needed to glow. Default 0, so energy does not gate it.
notes.edge_glow_width: The width of the emission along the edge, in pixels. The default 100 is wide because edge light on a real tube bleeds a long way inward.
notes.energy_curve: How speed bends into energy. 1.0 is linear.
notes.energy_dot_curve: The exponent of dwell saturation. The default 1.6 weights dwell more strongly than a linear 1.0.
notes.energy_dot_max: The energy ceiling for a dwell dot, independent of the line ceiling (3.2 against the line's 1.2 to 4).
notes.energy_dot_ref: The dwell normalisation reference for a dot, in microseconds. Default 30 us; below that, I x dt is linear.
notes.energy_dwell_cap: The ceiling on energy piling up when dots are deposited repeatedly on one spot.
notes.energy_infl: How strongly the derived model applies. 0 = display intensity only, 1 = entirely from the model. For sources with no current information (AVG/DVG and the like, which have only a Z value).
notes.energy_line_max: The energy ceiling for a line (phosphor saturation per unit area). Colour's 1.2 barely saturates; monochrome and Vectrex use 4 for headroom.
notes.energy_model: 0 = off, where n is display intensity as before. 1 enables derivation from speed and dwell.
notes.energy_obj_knee: The energy at which the object lift begins to act.
notes.energy_obj_lift: How much energy an object (a bullet, an explosion) is lifted by. 0 is off.
notes.energy_obj_max: The ceiling of the object lift.
notes.energy_obj_sharp: How sharply the object lift comes on. Larger means it lights up abruptly at the threshold.
notes.energy_obj_star: An extra lift for stars - isolated points.
notes.energy_speed_norm: The speed normalisation reference (screen widths per ms). The faster the beam, the shorter the dwell per point and the dimmer it is; this is the conversion factor.
notes.energy_stroke_agg: At 1, the average speed over a whole stroke (a continuous run from RAMP-on to RAMP-off) is used instead of each segment's own speed.
notes.flicker_blue_depth: How far cyclic flicker drops the blue channel. Blue phosphor is short-persistence, so it is set deeper.
notes.flicker_buckets: How many steps the carry-over is divided into. More is smoother, fewer is steppier.
notes.flicker_green_depth: How far cyclic flicker drops the green channel.
notes.flicker_period_ms: The time per step. Monochrome's 16.7 ms is one frame at 60 Hz.
notes.flicker_red_depth: How far cyclic flicker drops the red channel.
notes.flicker_thresh_ms: Flicker begins once one sweep takes longer than this to draw. A real AVG cannot finish too many vectors in one frame and carries them into the next, which is what flickers.
notes.glow_black_toe: A floor that cuts the dark end of the glow, removing weak glow to keep black tight.
notes.glow_fbo_scale: The resolution multiplier of the glow FBO - a performance control. 0.4 is 16% of the area. Glow is blurred to begin with, so lowering it costs little visually.
notes.glow_narrow: The strength of the narrow bloom stage. The defaults of 0.003 to 0.005 are tiny because bloom adds, so a little is enough.
notes.glow_tail_curve: How the glow's tail falls. Below 1 (monochrome's 0.6) the tail lingers; above 1 (colour's 1.44) it drops away quickly.
notes.glow_wide: The wide bloom stage, computed on a low-resolution target so it is cheap. The default is tiny - 0.00018 on monochrome.
notes.glow_wide_curve: The shaping curve of the wide glow. Above 1 it crushes dim glow and keeps only the bright parts.
notes.glow_wide_pivot: The reference level of that shaping. This level does not move; only above and below it bend.
notes.glow_wide_reach: How far the wide glow reaches - how many pyramid levels are used.
notes.glow_wide_smooth: How smooth the wide glow's downsampling is.
notes.halation_gain: The overall halation gain. The monochrome maximum is 5 because that turned out to be the real ceiling when [M] Halation Amount went from 3 to 5.
notes.halo_quad_extent: The size of the quad one analytic line is drawn into, as a multiple of sigma. Smaller is faster but clips a wide halo.
notes.hdr_glow_stability: Compensation that keeps the glow tail from thickening as beam_peak_nits is raised.
notes.hdr_rolloff_knee: Highlight roll-off, given as a multiple of peak. Rounding starts at the knee and saturates at max.
notes.hdr_rolloff_max: Highlight roll-off, given as a multiple of peak. Rounding starts at the knee and saturates at max.
notes.hdr_sat_protect: Protection for saturated colour. Clipping outright shifts the hue of a highly saturated colour; this is how much only the luminance is rounded, keeping the hue.
notes.hv_droop: The strength of the droop (dimming plus defocus). 0 disables it.
notes.hv_droop_dim: Whether the HV droop also dims. At 0 it shows only as loss of focus.
notes.hv_droop_onset: The load at which HV droop begins - the threshold past which a brighter screen pulls the supply down.
notes.hv_droop_ref: The reference that normalises load to 0..1. Smaller saturates sooner.
notes.intensity_overdrive: How much the overload adds to core brightness. 0 turns it off entirely.
notes.intensity_overdrive_curve: How that addition bends. The default 2 on monochrome and Vectrex makes it come on late.
notes.isolated_dot_min_size: The minimum size of an isolated dwell dot, in pixels, to keep a very small dot from vanishing.
notes.line_cap_mode: The shape of the line end (0 to 3). Every chain differs: colour 0, monochrome 1, Vectrex 2.
notes.line_cap_overload_add: The width in pixels added to the ends when overdriven - the way the ends of an explosion's lines swell in particular.
notes.line_cap_overload_curve: How that addition bends. Colour's 0.25 and monochrome/Vectrex's 4 are opposites: colour comes on early, the others late.
notes.line_cap_transition: The distance in pixels over which the body turns into the end. Longer makes the end swell more gradually.
notes.line_cap_width: The end width as a multiple of the body width. Above 1 the end swells, as a real tube's ends round off.
notes.line_point_threshold: The boundary, in pixels, below which a segment is treated as a point. Measured after layout and orientation, in a space that preserves the segment's true length.
notes.macro_beam_sim: A 0/1 toggle that removes the supply and deflection imperfections wholesale: beam jitter, HV droop, per-RGB flicker depth, the beam time window.
notes.macro_beam_width: Line thickness. Scales beam_width_min and beam_width_max (the widths of a dim and a bright line) and overload_width_add (the extra width when overdriven) together.
notes.macro_bezel: How much light the bezel - outside the edge of the tube face - returns. Default 0 is off; at 1.0, bezel_glow_strength and monitor_bezel_reflection take their JSON defaults.
notes.macro_bloom: A single multiplier over the three glow stages (glow_wide, glow_narrow, analytic_glow). 1.0 is the shipped look.
notes.macro_defocus: How much focus is lost. Scales defocus (across the face), edge_defocus (astigmatism at the edges from deflection angle) and overload_bloom (blur under overload) together.
notes.macro_exposure: The overall brightness of the beam. It scales beam_peak_nits under HDR and sdr_beam_level under SDR, so the same move works the same way in either.
notes.macro_halation: A single multiplier over halation (reflection rings inside the tube face) and starburst (the radial rays).
notes.macro_monitor_sim: A 0/1 toggle that removes the optics that are not the beam - the tube face, the glass and the bezel - wholesale.
notes.macro_overload: How burnt-in a draw that pins the Z axis (an explosion, a bullet) looks. Moves three sliders together along a curve, starting with overload_threshold, the energy above which something counts as overloaded.
notes.macro_persistence: How long the afterglow lasts. Scales phosphor_half_ms (the half-life) and phosphor_total_ms (until it is fully gone) together, so the decay curve keeps its shape and only its time axis stretches.
notes.macro_point_bright: The brightness of points (point_brightness_scale). A point covers little area and gets lost at the same luminance, so it is controlled separately from size.
notes.macro_point_size: The size of points: point_width_scale, and on Vectrex isolated_dot_min_size, the minimum size in pixels of an isolated dwell dot.
notes.mask_overdrive_flare: The strength of the white-hot core after it has passed through the shadow mask.
notes.masked_core_peak: The peak limit on the core as seen through the mask.
notes.mglow_brightness: Brightness. Outside the gate for the same reason.
notes.mglow_center_edge_diff: The difference in brightness between centre and edge. Outside the gate for the same reason.
notes.mglow_coefficient: The coefficient for monitor glow strength.
notes.mglow_coverage_full: Gated on screen coverage: the more beam goes off screen the brighter it glows, beginning at start and reaching maximum at full.
notes.mglow_coverage_start: Gated on screen coverage: the more beam goes off screen the brighter it glows, beginning at start and reaching maximum at full.
notes.mglow_min_distance: How far off screen the beam must go before the glow starts.
notes.mglow_rgb_band_count: The number of bands. Outside the gate because 0 does not mean off here - gating it would change the shape.
notes.mglow_rgb_bands: The RGB banding. At 0 the band term is exactly 1 and the glow comes out neutrally coloured.
notes.monitor_bezel_reflection: How much of the monitor glow the bezel returns. A separate path from the beam-derived reflection.
notes.overdrive_color: The colour of overdrive - where a pinned draw heads chromatically.
notes.overdrive_core: Whether the overload shows only as flare or in the core itself. 0 = flare only, the older behaviour.
notes.overdrive_knee: The overdrive knee and ceiling, as multiples of peak.
notes.overdrive_sat_curve: How saturation drains away under overdrive.
notes.overlap_white_brightness: The brightness of the overlap white-out.
notes.overlap_white_count: Roughly how many overlapping lines it takes to count as white-hot.
notes.overlap_white_spread: How far the overlap white-out spreads.
notes.overlap_white_strength: How strongly a place where lines cross goes white-hot. It responds to several lines overlapping, not to one very bright line.
notes.overlay_ambient_light: Ambient light falling on the overlay. Gated by [M] Monitor/Glass Sim.
notes.overlay_color_dark_level: The dark level of the coloured resin - the floor below which it does not go fully black.
notes.overlay_color_density: The optical density of the coloured resin. Higher is a deeper colour and passes less light. Default 1.75.
notes.overlay_color_glow: Scatter from the resin's back face - light spreads behind the coloured resin too. Default 1.1.
notes.overlay_color_highlight_bleach: Colour draining out in bright areas: strong light through coloured resin saturates and reads as white. bleach is how much drains (default 0 = off), knee where it starts, curve how it bends.
notes.overlay_color_highlight_curve: Colour draining out in bright areas: strong light through coloured resin saturates and reads as white. bleach is how much drains (default 0 = off), knee where it starts, curve how it bends.
notes.overlay_color_highlight_knee: Colour draining out in bright areas: strong light through coloured resin saturates and reads as white. bleach is how much drains (default 0 = off), knee where it starts, curve how it bends.
notes.overlay_diffusion_shape: The shape of the diffusion. The default 0.4 is concentrated close in with a short tail.
notes.overlay_white_diffusion: How strongly the white resin diffuses - the beam bleeds as it passes through the overlay.
notes.overlay_white_reflectance: The reflectance of the white areas: the component that makes the overlay itself look bright by reflecting room light.
notes.overlay_white_transmission: Transmission through the white areas. The default 0.65 is a measured value.
notes.overload_bloom: Extra blur under overload. Scaled by [M] Defocus.
notes.overload_core_gain: The strength of the white-hot core under overload - what is added to the core as direct emission.
notes.overload_display_compression: How much overloaded energy is compressed on the display side.
notes.overload_dot_gain: A bias toward dwell dots. A stopped beam (a zero-length point) concentrates its energy on one spot, so at the same n it looks far hotter than a swept line or a text stroke.
notes.overload_glow_width: How far that glow spreads, in pixels.
notes.overload_max: The overdrive ceiling, as a multiple of peak. Default 3.
notes.overload_ramp: The energy span from threshold to full effect. Narrow gives a sudden onset, wide a gradual one.
notes.overload_threshold: The energy above which something counts as overloaded. Lowering it treats more as overloaded. Colour 1, monochrome 0.55 and Vectrex 0.3 differ this much because their sources' energy distributions do.
notes.overload_width_add: The width in pixels added to the core under overload.
notes.overload_width_bloom_link: How tightly overload width and bloom are linked.
notes.overload_width_center: The centre of the overload width's onset.
notes.overload_width_steepness: How sharply the overload width comes on.
notes.phosphor_color: The emission colour of the phosphor. Monochrome's [0.9, 0.9, 1] is a slightly blue P4; Vectrex's [0.5, 0.7, 1] is the real machine's blue-green tube.
notes.phosphor_curve: The shape of the decay curve (the Hill exponent p). Larger means bright for a while, then a sudden fall.
notes.phosphor_energy_decay: Two-phase decay. The normal part (<= 1) uses the base half-life and the overrange part (> 1) decays this many times faster; the two are summed.
notes.phosphor_half_ms: How long the afterglow takes to fall to half brightness - the main determinant of how long persistence feels. Colour's 16 ms is an AVG colour tube, monochrome's 24 ms a P4, Vectrex's 16 ms measured.
notes.phosphor_hit_reset: The floor above which new light counts as re-excitation and resets the age to 0.
notes.phosphor_hold_ms: How long full brightness is held before the decay begins. With a short half-life calibrated for a trail-like look, the afterglow falls to about 27% within one present interval, leaving seams between the successive positions of a slow bright line.
notes.phosphor_overdrive: How far peak excitation swings to white - strong excitation losing its colour and going white-hot.
notes.phosphor_rgb_combination: How bright RGB is when combined in one place. 0 normalises to peak, 1 adds physically.
notes.phosphor_rgb_combination_width: How much a line appears to thicken where RGB combines.
notes.phosphor_rgb_decay: Per-channel multipliers on phosphor persistence, expressing blue being short and green long.
notes.phosphor_total_ms: How long until it reaches zero. Its ratio to the half-life sets how stretched the curve really is. Monochrome's 800 ms assumes a long-persistence tube.
notes.phosphor_weak_hit_composite: Keeps a weak redraw from darkening brighter afterglow that is still there.
notes.point_brightness_scale: The brightness multiplier for points. A point covers little area and is lost at the same luminance; this compensates.
notes.point_roundness: How round a point is. 0 is the same cross-section as a line, 1 a perfect circle.
notes.point_width_scale: The width multiplier for points. Colour's 1.8 makes points read thicker than lines; monochrome's 0.6 does the opposite.
notes.primary_blue_brightness: Blue. The label reads Blue Hue Shift (Violet +), so positive is toward violet.
notes.primary_blue_hue: Blue. The label reads Blue Hue Shift (Violet +), so positive is toward violet.
notes.primary_blue_saturation: Blue. The label reads Blue Hue Shift (Violet +), so positive is toward violet.
notes.primary_color_mode: 0 = specified as chromaticity (chroma_*), 1 = specified as HSB (primary_*).
notes.primary_red_brightness: Red hue shift in degrees, saturation and brightness. The default saturation of 0.85 is shallower than sRGB: a real red phosphor is not as saturated as the sRGB primary.
notes.primary_red_hue: Red hue shift in degrees, saturation and brightness. The default saturation of 0.85 is shallower than sRGB: a real red phosphor is not as saturated as the sRGB primary.
notes.primary_red_saturation: Red hue shift in degrees, saturation and brightness. The default saturation of 0.85 is shallower than sRGB: a real red phosphor is not as saturated as the sRGB primary.
notes.radial_converge_blue: Blue beam misregistration in the radial direction, growing or shrinking with distance from the centre.
notes.radial_converge_green: Green beam misregistration in the radial direction, growing or shrinking with distance from the centre.
notes.radial_converge_red: Red beam misregistration in the radial direction, growing or shrinking with distance from the centre.
notes.ray_angle: The reference angle of the rays, default 15 degrees, matched to the orientation of the real glass structure.
notes.ray_count_rand: Randomisation over time - length and count vary frame to frame, so it does not read as a fixed static pattern.
notes.ray_gain: The gain of the radial rays. The default is tiny, around 0.005.
notes.ray_length_rand: Randomisation over time - length and count vary frame to frame, so it does not read as a fixed static pattern.
notes.ray_var: How much the rays vary in strength. Real rays are not uniform.
notes.ring_fill: The strength of the fill inside the ring. Outline and fill are separate because a real tube shows a thin bright ring and a faint disc inside it as two things.
notes.ring_gain: The strength of the ring's outline.
notes.ring_min_dwell: The minimum dwell needed to produce a ring, in microseconds. Default 20 us.
notes.ring_over_gain: How the ring responds to overdrive. The maximum of 20 is large because a strong ring is sometimes wanted on explosions alone.
notes.ring_radius: The radius of the ring - 44 px on monochrome, 30 px on Vectrex. It corresponds to the thickness of the glass.
notes.ring_threshold: The gate on the brightness side. Default 0, so brightness does not restrict it.
notes.room_ambient: How bright the room is. It affects how the overlay and the bezel look.
notes.sdr_beam_level: Beam exposure in SDR. Scaled by [M] Beam Brightness - the same macro as HDR's beam_peak_nits, so the same move works the same way in either.
notes.sdr_rolloff_ceiling: SDR highlight roll-off, as a multiple of white. Roll-off is disabled when ceiling <= knee.
notes.sdr_rolloff_knee: SDR highlight roll-off, as a multiple of white. Roll-off is disabled when ceiling <= knee.
notes.sdr_shadow_curve: The SDR shadow curve. Below 1 it lifts the dark end. Default 0.95.
notes.shadow_mask_brightboost: Compensation for the brightness the mask costs. Default 0, so none.
notes.shadow_mask_scale: The mask pitch, in pixels referred to 1080p.
notes.shadow_mask_strength: How dense the shadow mask is. 0 is no mask. Gated 0/1 by [M] Monitor/Glass Sim.
notes.tube_distortion: Distortion from the tube face's curvature (pincushion). Negative gives barrel.
notes.tube_face_scale: The size of the tube face (the glass) as a fraction of the window. vector_image_scale is how much of that the vector image occupies, so the two nest.
notes.tube_round_corner: How rounded the corners of the tube face are. A real tube has rounded corners.
notes.vector_image_scale: The scale of the vector image, which is not the same as tube_face_scale: it is how much of the tube face the image occupies, expressing a real machine that does not draw right out to the edge of the glass.
notes.vector_linearity_x: Deflection linearity (gain). 1.0 is ideal. A real machine differs slightly between X and Y, so a square reads as a rectangle.
notes.vector_linearity_y: Deflection linearity (gain). 1.0 is ideal. A real machine differs slightly between X and Y, so a square reads as a rectangle.
notes.vector_pincushion_x_quad: Asymmetric pincushion in X (quadratic). 0 is off. Where tube_distortion comes from the curvature of the face, this comes from non-linearity in the deflection.
notes.vertex_dwell: Vertex brightness from the beam slowing at a corner - on a real machine the corners look brighter. Colour defaults to 0.5; monochrome and Vectrex use 0 and handle it by other means.
notes.width_curve: How the energy-to-width response bends. Above 1 the middle is thinner and reaches maximum later, below 1 the middle is thicker, 1.0 is linear.
notes.width_knee: The fraction of the width already reached at the threshold T. Gentle up to T, then steep beyond it.
notes.width_over_curve: How width grows past the threshold. 1.0 is a straight line; larger makes it swell late.
notes.width_sigmoid: An S-curve applied on top of the width curve. Positive is sharper, negative gentler, 0 off.
notes.width_sigmoid_center: The inflection point of the width S-curve.
notes.z_rise_tau: The rise time of the Z amplifier. A draw with a short dwell ends before Z has risen, so it is dim.
